title: Cohort Margin & Temp-Hire Swapbook — Sep 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick working workbook and playbook to align headcount phasing with per-cohort pricing sensitivity and run discrete 'temp-hire swap' scenarios for Q4 2026 / H1 2027. This is intentionally operational (notes + scratch calc) rather than a polished model.

Summary of approach:
- Break revenue into three customer cohorts: Startups (S), Mid-market (M), Enterprise (E).
- For each cohort model unit economics at 3 price points: Base, -15% (aggressive promotional), +10% (premium).
- Simulate headcount mix changes (perm hires vs. temp contractors) and compute margin delta under throughput shocks (token demand +30% and -20%).
- Define simple trigger rules for converting temp->perm or swapping perm->temp based on 6-week rolling utilization and 12-week cost forecast.

High-level assumptions (working):
- Gross margin baseline by cohort at current staffing: S=42%, M=48%, E=55%.
- Token mix: embeddings 25%, generation 60%, fine-tuning/ops 15%.
- Average cost per token (infrastructure + infra staff allocation) baseline: $0.0009/token.
- Average revenue per token by cohort (Base): S=$0.0014, M=$0.0018, E=$0.0023.
- Temp contractor loaded cost = perm * 1.25 (short-term premium), but adjustable headcount ramp faster (2–4 weeks to full productivity).
- One perm engineer fully allocated to serving/runtime supports ~120k tokens/min sustained across routes; contractor supports ~70% of that.

Scratch scenario outputs (rounded):
1) Base price, +30% demand shock, no headcount change:
   - S margin -> 30% (drop 12ppt), M -> 36% (drop 12ppt), E -> 43% (drop 12ppt)
   - Burn increases: incremental infra $720k/mo; infra ops overtime and on-call increases pay by ~$90k/mo.

2) Base price, +30% demand, swap 6 perm hires -> 9 temp contractors (fast ramp):
   - Near-term margin improvement vs. no-swap: +5ppt across cohorts (helpful), but 2-monthly expected perm rehire cost if churn grows.
   - Net monthly cash delta: save ~$210k/mo versus hiring perm (accounting for contractor premium and reduced ramp).

3) -15% price across S cohort (targeted promo), demand +50% for S, other cohorts flat:
   - S revenue per token declines; margin falls to ~18% but revenue rises enough to net positive contribution in month 1 for Net new S demand > 40% (threshold found in the sensitivity grid).
   - Cross-cohort cannibalization observed in model if promo > -20% (users upgrade/downgrade routes).

Sensitivity grid (high level notes):
- Price elasticity (S): strong. A -10% price -> +22% token demand on avg; -15% -> +37% demand.
- Price elasticity (M): muted. -10% -> +8% demand; -15% -> +13% demand.
- Price elasticity (E): negligible short-term; discounts primarily used in committed capacity negotiations.
- Margins are most sensitive to infra-per-token cost (kernel choices / quantization). A $0.00015/token improvement yields ~3–5ppt margin lift depending on cohort mix.

Headcount phasing playbook (practical triggers):
- Trigger A (scale-up, short): 6-week rolling capacity > 85% AND 6-week revenue growth > +18% -> hire contractors or apply fast temp-hire swap (target 6–12 weeks coverage).
- Trigger B (convert): contractors > 6 months and sustained utilization > 70% OR forecasted 12-week incremental margin positive -> convert subset to perm (ratio 2:3 contractors->perm).
- Trigger C (contractor rollback): 8-week projected demand decline > -15% -> don't renew contractor contracts and freeze perm hiring for 12 weeks.

Operational levers and quick experiments to reduce infra-per-token cost (ordered by expected impact):
1) Short sequence quantization trial on high-frequency routes (S & M) — target savings $0.00008/token for those routes.
2) Route-level prefix caching for Top-10 customers (E cohort) — reduces repeated tokens and cuts infra load ~6–9%.
3) Model mix nudges: shift low-value routes to smaller quantized variants with auto-fallback for E customers.
4) Temporary burst capacity commit in one region rather than multi-region burst — saves ~12% on short-term reserve costs but increases tail-latency risk.

Financial guardrails (recommended):
- Maintain 10% buffer in headcount hiring budget for contractor premium (assume 25% uplift).
- Set a runway-friendly threshold: only convert contractors to perm if 12-week forecast shows net positive cumulative margin after amortized conversion cost.
- Pricing experiments should have automatic kill-switch: if M cohort margin drops >8ppt for 4 consecutive weeks, revert pricing or apply targeted countermeasures.

Open questions / data needs (short backlog):
- Need route-level per-token cost broken out by model variant + quantization (pull from infra-metering team).
- Updated elasticity estimates per cohort by product (chat vs. embed vs. fine-tune).
- Contractor productivity profiles by role (serving infra vs. platform) from SRE/eng leads.
- Legal/Proc notes: variable contractor agreements should include 2-week ramp clauses to avoid long tail cost exposure.

Immediate next steps (owner + timeframe):
- Priya: sync with infra-metering (Daniel) by 2026-09-10 to import route-level token cost.
- Lina: run cohort-level price experiment design doc and kill-switch thresholds by 2026-09-17.
- Samir: draft temp-hire contract template with procurement & legal by 2026-09-24.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working swapbook — please comment inline on the elasticity assumptions and any known upcoming contract renewals that would affect capacity.
- If approved, finance will convert selected scenarios into a line-itemed P&L addendum for Oct–Dec planning.

Appendix (quick table of scenario P&L deltas, rounded):
- Base +30% demand, no-change: incremental revenue +$1.2M/mo, incremental cost +$0.9M/mo, margin delta -12ppt cohort average.
- Base +30% demand, temp-swap: incremental revenue +$1.2M/mo, incremental cost +$0.65M/mo, cash delta +$250k/mo vs no-swap.
- S promo -15% (aggressive) with +50% demand: incremental revenue +$180k/mo, incremental cost +$120k/mo, immediate margin negative for first 4 weeks but positive cumulative after month 2 if retention >= 72%.

(End of working sheet)
